title: Ivo and the Salt
premise: Ines Oyelaran, last apprentice of the Saltmakers' Guild, sells harmless charms in Vellagard, a city where magic was outlawed after the gods went silent and the dragons were hunted to one. When prayers begin to be answered again—wildly, dangerously—Ines discovers the old gods are returning through cracks only he can see, because his guild's salt was always the seal that kept them out. Hunted by the Inquisitor who killed his master, Ines joins a found family of smugglers, heretics, and the last dragon's keeper to reach the Door of Ash, the threshold out of a country that legally no longer exists. He ends the ban not by restoring magic but by renegotiating it: the gods return on terms written in salt and signed in blood, and Ines finally belongs—to a guild reborn as something new.
about_author: M. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write about outlawed wonders from a house with too many keys.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Ines sells luck-knots and fever-salts in Vellagard's night market, hiding his guild sigil beneath his sleeve. A desperate mother buys a charm that shouldn't work—and does. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a gift practiced in secret, and the first tremor of dread when the impossible happens.

chapters.title: The Guild of Nine Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Ines returns to the Saltmakers' ruined hall and speaks to the nine chairs of dead masters, reporting the working charm. His master's ghost-note warns him: if the salt fails, everything sealed comes home. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief braided with responsibility; he realizes he inherited a duty, not just a trade.

chapters.title: What the Prayers Bought
chapters.summary: Across the city, answered prayers turn monstrous—a fisherman's wish drowns his street; a child's prayer for rain floods a chapel. The Inquisition posts new edicts. POV: Sergeant Odile Ferrant, a reluctant Inquisition officer. Emotional beat: mounting civic terror, and Odile's first doubt about the justice she serves.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Ines tests the city's boundary stones and finds the sealing salt corroded through—someone has been unsealing the country deliberately. He is nearly caught by Odile but escapes through smuggler tunnels. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Ines seeks Brannoc Vale, a smuggler who once owed Ines's master a life-debt, and finds instead Brannoc's crew: a defrocked priestess, a forger, and a mute boy who hears gods. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: reluctant hospitality hardening into alliance; the first sketch of found family.

chapters.title: Edict of Nothingness
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: twelve years ago, the Crown declared the old kingdom dissolved, erasing its laws, names, and gods—legally, the country never existed. Young Ines watches his master sign the guild's surrender. POV: Ines (past). Emotional beat: the wound at the story's heart—how a people can be legislated out of belonging.

chapters.title: The Keeper Below
chapters.summary: The crew descends to the ash-caves where Serevan, the last dragon, gutters like a dying lamp, kept alive by an exiled keeper named Tamsin. The dragon recognizes Ines's salt-blood. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: awe and tenderness; Ines learns the fire keeping the seals intact is almost spent.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Halden's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's superior, Inquisitor Halden, reveals he has been feeding prayers to the cracks himself, believing returned gods will legitimize the new regime—if he controls them. Odile sees the trap. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: cold ambition versus conscience; she begins quietly sabotaging him.

chapters.title: A Market Burned
chapters.summary: Halden purges the night market to find the 'salt-witch.' Ines's customers and neighbors are taken; the mute boy, Pell, is nearly among them. Ines chooses exposure over escape, using real magic publicly to shield them. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the moment hiding stops being survivable or forgivable.

chapters.title: Outlawed Together
chapters.summary: Branded and hunted, Ines takes refuge with Brannoc's crew in the drowned chapel. Around a smuggled fire, each shares what they lost to the Edict of Nothingness. POV: rotating within the crew. Emotional beat: the found family crystallizes—not born of blood but of shared erasure.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: A god slips through a crack and offers Ines restoration of the guild in exchange for resealing the Door forever—abandoning everyone else outside. Ines refuses. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation and integrity; justice must be for all, not a private bargain.

chapters.title: Maps of a Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: The forger, Wren, reconstructs the erased kingdom's maps from memory, songs, and gravestones, locating the Door of Ash beneath the old coronation field. Odile, now fugitive, arrives with Halden's plans. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: reclamation—naming what was erased makes it real again.

chapters.title: What Odile Saw
chapters.summary: Odile recounts the massacre she witnessed during the Purge Years and why she stayed silent; the crew must decide whether to trust her. Tamsin vouches for her. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: shame met with imperfect grace; trust as a choice, not a verdict.

chapters.title: March Through the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: The company crosses the blinding salt flats toward the Door while Halden's riders pursue. Pell collapses; Serevan's fading fire shields them in a final aerial pass that costs the dragon dearly. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: endurance and cost; every mile is paid for.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Serevan lands broken. Tamsin reveals the truth: the dragon-fire isn't failing naturally—Halden's agents have been siphoning it to control which gods return. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak; the dying light was murdered slowly.

chapters.title: Terms in Salt
chapters.summary: At the Door of Ash, Ines drafts new covenant terms using guild rites: gods may return bound to consent, witness, and answerability—magic under law they help write. The assembled gods listen because the salt remembers every oath ever sworn upon it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terrified authority; the apprentice becomes the guild.

chapters.title: Halden at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Halden arrives with an army and demands the Door open to his chosen pantheon alone. Odile arrests him with her own warrant, invoking the erased kingdom's law—which, she argues, still binds anyone claiming its throne's authority. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: justice reclaimed from within the system that betrayed her.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: To fuel the covenant, the Door needs living flame. Serevan gives the last of his fire willingly, and the gods, honoring the gift, kindle him anew from their side—dragon and divine made mutually sustaining. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief transfigured; death refused by reciprocity.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: Ines signs the covenant in salt and blood before witnesses: the crew, Odile, the freed prisoners, and the gods themselves. The Edict of Nothingness burns off the archive-stone; the country exists again, renamed by those it erased. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: catharsis—belonging granted not by decree but by signature.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Magic returns lawfully; charms are licensed by the reborn guild, now open to all comers including former Inquisitors seeking penance. Brannoc's crew becomes its first wardens. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: cautious joy; the world is better but watchful.

chapters.title: Nine Chairs Filled
chapters.summary: In the restored hall, the guild seats nine new masters—including Odile, Tamsin, Wren, and Pell. Ines takes the tenth chair, newly carved, marked 'Apprentice, Retired.' POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fullness; the empty chairs that haunted him are filled by chosen family.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Salt
chapters.summary: Years later, Ines teaches apprentices at the market stall where he once hid his sigil, sleeves rolled, mark shown proudly. A frightened child asks if the gods really answer now. 'Yes,' he says, 'and we answer back.' POV: Ines. Emotional beat: peace earned; the circle closed, the door held open.
